cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Brighter Side
cards.instruction: Meet every setback with even greater optimism.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's handle this professionally. Our show sold no tickets. We can rehearse uninterrupted.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The theatre's cancelled us. I'm asking for our deposit back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can explain the standard again. Slowly. Even better! We'll hire the pub upstairs. People already go there voluntarily.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've kept the deposit. All we can afford is the bus home.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful—a touring production! I'll carry the scenery; you bring exact change. We can try the opening scene between stops.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 and A3 optimism is clear, but professional wrappers do not shape A production decisions through exacting correction.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 cancellation leads to A3 pub; B4 lost deposit leads to A5 bus touring plan.

relationship.evidence: B2 seeks money back and B4 states the remaining travel budget, trying to end a failed show.

heightening.evidence: A5 converts B4 bus home into a touring venue with an actual task for B.

specificity.evidence: A1 no ticket sales and B4 only bus fare supply clear losses and stakes.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 standard-again phrase is unrelated to venue selection.
